# supervisor

Supervisor mode: sessions that plan and delegate, enforced by the harness.

- **Runs in:** the harness process
- **Source:** [lisp/modules/harness-supervisor.el](../../lisp/modules/harness-supervisor.el)
- **Loaded:** when enabled (see `harness-enable-modules`)
- **Requires:** [session](session.md), [agent](agent.md), [tools](tools.md), [readonly](readonly.md)
- **Brings along:** [ui-supervisor](ui-supervisor.md) (its UI)

## About

Supervisor mode makes a top-level session on an expensive model plan
and coordinate while cheaper models do the work.  A prompt that says
"delegate, don't do" is ignored often enough that the harness
enforces the rule itself.  A session that supervises has

- no write tools: it is a read-only session (harness-readonly.el,
  which the module's policy `harness-supervisor--policy` tells about
  it), so `agent/tools` offers it only an allowlist (reading, the web,
  coordination, and the supervisor's own tools), and that module's
  `permission/decide` stage at 8 denies, for good, a call to anything
  else.  The stage is what holds when the model still has an old tool
  list, right after the user switched the mode on;
- only read-only, offline bash, and only when the sandbox can confine
  commands (`sandbox/confined-p`): that module's `tools/sandbox-options`
  filter makes every command run with every directory read-only and no
  network.  The elisp tool's background Emacs is such a command too, so
  the elisp tool, which the allowlist leaves out, would run so all the same;
- a turn that may end only on a decision.  The `agent/stop` filter
  sends a model that stopped without one back, twice at most, with a
  reminder; after that it lets the turn end and leaves a hint.

A plan is approved by the user alone, and only in ask mode.  It
changes nothing by itself: every call of its workers goes through the
whole permission chain in the worker's own session, and that
session's mode and judge decide it as usual.  So `submit_plan` and
`retry_step` ask the user only in ask mode, with the user present
(the session not non-interactive).  In accept-edits, auto and yolo
mode, and in any non-interactive session whatever its mode, the
`permission/decide` stage at 28 allows them, after the mode and the
rules (20) and before the judge (30), so that the auto-mode judge never
rules on a plan.  What an earlier stage denied stays denied: the
refusals of the readonly module's stage at 8, a standing deny rule.
`no_plan_needed` only records a decision, and is allowed in every mode.

Whether a session supervises is its `:ext` `:supervisor`: t, `:false`
for hands-on, or nothing for a session this module does not govern
(a sub-agent, a side conversation, a session older than the module).
It is set when the session is created, so the chat header shows it
from the start (`session/created`): a top-level session takes the
setting `harness-supervisor` has for its directory, a task's session
`harness-supervisor-tasks` (`task/changed`; the session that writes a
backlog task up only reads, and takes the setting when the task
starts, a planned task's working hands-on since its plan is made),
and a fork its parent's value.  Only the user changes it
later, with `supervisor/set` for one session or `supervisor/set-all`
for every governed one: there is no tool for it.  A change
takes effect at the next tool call, since the permission stage reads
the live session, and at the next step for the tool list.

A supervising turn is also watched for length.  A turn that makes
`harness-supervisor-step-budget` tool calls is steered to submit its
plan with what it knows, and again every half budget after that.  It
is a nudge, never a stop.

The system prompt of a supervising session says how the mode works,
in place of the Planning section.

The plan engine is what the supervisor decides with.  Its tools are named
in `harness-supervisor-tools` and `harness-supervisor-decision-tools`,
so the gates above apply to them.  `submit_plan` takes a list of steps,
each a self-contained job with a tier (simple or medium), a context
(fresh or fork) and the steps it waits for.  A plan has no hard step:
the supervisor plans on its provider's hard model, and breaks the work
down until every step is medium at most, so that the strong model
decides and the cheaper ones carry it out; only `retry_step` runs a
step on hard, when its worker was not up to it.  `submit_plan` refuses
a plan with problems, naming each, and otherwise records the plan,
shows it as the `plan` tool shows one, starts the steps that are ready
and ends the turn.  A step runs in a worker, a session of its own with
the full tool set, on the model of its tier: `harness-supervisor-tiers`,
else the supervisor's provider's model of the tier of the same name
(`provider/tier-model`: simple, medium, hard; never frontier, which is
the user's to pick).  A provider whose catalogue has not answered
yet is waited for, briefly (`harness-supervisor--tier-wait`), so a slow
listing does not read as a provider with no model for the tier; only one
that truly names none gives the step the supervisor's own model, and the
hint says which provider it is and why (the step keeps the reason as
`:model-fallback`).  A step is fresh by default: a new session in the
supervisor's directory, whose first message holds the plan's summary
(what every step shares), its own prompt and the plan's other steps.
A fork step forks the supervisor at the call that submitted the plan,
a node every step of the plan shares, and only while that conversation
is short: no fork reads its parent's prompt cache (its system prompt
and tools differ, and its model usually does), so a fork writes the
whole conversation into its model's cache and reads it again on every
call.  Past `harness-supervisor-fork-limit` tokens of it
(`harness-supervisor--conversation-tokens`, recorded on the plan as
`:fork-tokens`) `submit_plan` refuses fork steps, and a fork step of
an older plan past it starts from a compaction
(`harness-supervisor--compact-fork`).  When a plan has two or more
fork steps on one model they all fork through one seed (`seed/fork`),
so that the context is written to that model's prompt cache once.  The
window of both is capped as `harness-tools-agent-context-limit` says,
and never silently: a hint in the worker's transcript says so
(`harness-supervisor--limit-hint`).  The worker's reply is the step's
result, which the steps that wait for it are given.  A worker shows
in the supervisor's transcript as the `spawn_agent` call that would
have started it -- the call when it starts, its result when the step
ends -- recorded by the harness (`harness-outside-node-p`), so the
supervisor's model never sees it and nothing waits for it.

Thinking goes with the tier.  A provider's tiers may name the level
each runs its model at (`provider/tier-thinking`: DeepSeek runs Flash
at low for simple, high for medium and max for hard).  A session that
supervises has its thinking raised to the level of its provider's hard
tier, and back to what it was when the mode is turned off; a worker
thinks at the level of its step's tier (`harness-supervisor-tiers`,
else its model's provider), so the many small steps cost less thinking
than the plan, and at its supervisor's when the tier names none.
Either way the level is fitted to what the worker's model offers
(`provider/fit-thinking`).  A provider whose tiers name no level, as
Claude's, keeps the old behavior: sessions think as they were
configured, and workers as their supervisor does.

A step that starts again -- `retry_step`, perhaps on a higher tier, or an
interrupted step after a restart -- decides its context by the cache.  A
fork never shares its parent's cache (its system prompt names its own
directories, its tool list differs), and a retry on a higher tier runs
on a model that has never read the plan's conversation, so forking the
supervisor would send all of it uncached at that model's price, and the
cowboy's gate (harness-cowboy.el) never sees a new fork as cold.  So
with a warm seed for the plan's node on the step's model (`seed/warm-p`)
the worker forks through it, as above, and reads the shared context from
the cache.  Without one it forks the supervisor directly and the fork is
compacted before its first turn, as the cowboy would for a session
nobody is asked about (`cowboy/compact`, its default, a brief summary
unless the user chose otherwise; with no cowboy, a brief summary from
`compaction/compact`; with no compaction, the whole conversation).  A
compaction that fails fails nothing.  Either way the supervisor gets a
hint saying which, and the worker's message says its conversation was
compacted.  The step keeps the attempt before as `:previous` (`:attempt
:session :model :error'), which the worker's message points at: it can
read what was tried with session_read, and should not repeat what
failed.  A fork step of a plan past `harness-supervisor-fork-limit` is
compacted the same way on its first attempt too, seed or not.  Other
first attempts, and fresh steps, decide as before.

The plans of a session are its `:ext` `:supervisor-plans`, so they
survive a restart and the UI shows them: each change of a step is a
`session/ext-changed`.  A plan has `:id :title :summary :node :call-id
:created :fork-tokens :steps', a step `:id :title :prompt :tier
:reason :context :after :model :state :session :attempts :result
:error', `:thinking` when its tier names a level, and, once it ran,
`:worker-model` (the model of its worker), `:ended` (when its last
attempt ended) and, once it started again, `:previous`.  A step of a
plan stored before the tiers were renamed has mundane or standard as
its tier, which read as simple and medium.  A step whose tier found
no model keeps `:model-fallback`, the reason (`unknown`, `unlisted`
or `none`), and runs on the supervisor's own model.  A step is
pending, running, done, failed, interrupted, cancelled or superseded:
a new plan supersedes the steps of the earlier ones that have not
started, and their running steps finish as usual.

What the supervisor hears.  A step that is done is a hint, and starts
the steps that waited for it.  A step that did not get done -- its
worker could not be made or its turn failed, was cancelled or blocked
(it is failed), or its worker session was deleted (cancelled) -- is a
message of its own, from the harness: the step, its tier and
model, why, the steps held on it, and the ways on (`retry_step`,
perhaps on a higher tier; a new plan; the user).  Steps interrupted
together, as their task went back to the queue, share one message.
When the last step of a plan is done the message lists each step with
its result and asks the supervisor to check the work and decide.  An
idle session starts a turn on a message and a running turn is steered;
one that arrives while the turn that submitted the plan is ending would
be lost with it, so it waits for the turn's end.  `retry_step` runs a
step again on a new worker, and does not end the turn.

A task's supervisor hands the work in as done only once it is.  The
stage at 8 refuses, for good, a `hand_in` without `cannot_continue`
while a step of the session's plans is open
(`harness-supervisor--open-steps`): pending or running, or ended
without being done -- failed, interrupted or cancelled -- until
`retry_step` gets it done or a plan submitted after it ended replaces
it, which is what a step keeps `:ended` for.  The refusal names the
open steps and the ways on: run one again, replace it with a new plan,
wait for one that runs, or give the task up with `hand_in` and
`cannot_continue`, which is never refused.  The user can still approve
the refused call in the chat, as any denial.  The report of a step
that did not get done tells a task's supervisor so, and so does its
system prompt.

Work that runs outside the turn is `agent/outstanding` for the tasks
module, which keeps the task of the session working, with a line of what
it waits for, instead of ending it in review: steps running, and pending
steps that can still start.  A step held behind one that did not get
done is not counted: the supervisor was told and has to decide.  It is
`agent/stop-outstanding` too, which stops that work.

When the harness restarts its workers die.  Once every module is up,
the steps still stored as running are interrupted and reported as a
failure is: to the session of a task as a message, so that the task
carries on, and to any other session queued, to go with the user's next
message rather than start an expensive turn unasked.  A task pre-empted
or returned to the queue has its running steps interrupted the same
way, once no turn of its session runs (`agent/stop-outstanding`, which
says why): their workers are cancelled, with the sub-agents they
started, a worker still being made is never given its step, and the
steps are reported in one message, which waits in the transcript while
the task waits in the queue (`harness-supervisor--stop-outstanding`).
Nothing starts again on its own: the steps held on them wait for the
supervisor.  A worker's late end changes nothing, as the step no longer
runs that attempt.
Deleting a supervisor cancels its workers, and turning the mode off
lets them carry on.

## Provides

### Methods

- `supervisor/act` (session-id node-id action) — Do the next thing the judge's note NODE-ID of SESSION-ID offers.
- `supervisor/active-p` (session-id) — Return non-nil when session SESSION-ID supervises.
- `supervisor/get` (session-id) — Return the supervisor setting of session SESSION-ID: t, `:false` or nil.
- `supervisor/set` (session-id on) — Turn supervisor mode on or off for session SESSION-ID; return its plist.
- `supervisor/set-all` (on &optional filter) — Turn supervisor mode on or off for every governed session FILTER selects.

### Tools

- `no_plan_needed` — Say that this turn needs no plan, with a one-line reason: you answered a question, there is nothing to do, or a plan you submitted is still running. It ends your turn's duty to decide, not the turn: give your reply after it. Work that changes files always goes in a plan (submit_plan), however small: you cannot change files yourself, and a worker makes the change.
- `retry_step` — Run a step of a submitted plan again on a new worker: a step that failed, was interrupted (by a restart, or when its task went back to the queue), or was cancelled. step is its id. plan is the id of its plan and defaults to the latest plan that has the step. tier moves the step to another tier, usually a higher one, when its model was not up to it: simple, medium, or hard, the model you run on, which only a retry reaches; a step that was too big is better split up in a new plan. reason says in a line why. prompt adds notes to the step's prompt for the new worker, such as what went wrong the first time. The steps held on the step start once it is done. It does not end your turn, so you can retry several steps in one message.
- `submit_plan` — Submit the plan for the work and start its workers. Call it once you know enough to plan; it is your decision for the turn whenever the work changes files, however small. summary is the plan in markdown, shown to the user and given to every fresh worker: the approach, what the steps share (interfaces, names, data shapes, which step makes each), and how the result is verified. Each step is a discrete unit of work for a worker on a cheaper model, which has the full tool set that you lack: an id (short, unique), a title, a prompt, a tier with a one-line reason, a context and after. The prompt is the step's brief, at the length its tier needs: for medium, a ticket (the goal, the constraints, the decisions you made, the files it owns, how to verify, what to report), whose worker reads the code it needs itself; for simple, the edits spelled out file by file. Say when the step must commit. The tier is simple for mechanical, well-specified edits and medium for the rest. A plan has no hard steps: you run on the hard model, and work that would need it is not broken down enough, so make the hard decisions yourself and write them into the prompts; a worker that is not up to its step can be run again on hard with retry_step. The context is fresh (the default: the worker starts with the summary, its prompt and the reports of the steps it waits for) or fork (it inherits this conversation as well, refused once the conversation is long, since a fork writes all of it into its worker model's cache). after lists the steps that must be done first; steps with no order between them run at once in the same working tree, so give them different files. The harness starts the steps that are ready, tells you in a new message when a step fails and when the plan has finished, and ends this turn now. A problem with the plan (an id used twice, an after that names no step, a cycle, a hard or unknown tier, an unknown context, a blank prompt, a fork of a long conversation) is returned as an error and nothing starts: fix it and call again.

### Events

- `supervisor/changed` — (SESSION-ID ON) when the user turned supervisor mode on (ON t) or off (ON :false) for a session

### Options

- `harness-supervisor` — How new top-level sessions start: supervising, hands-on, or judged.
- `harness-supervisor-fork-limit` — Most tokens of conversation a worker of a plan may inherit by forking.
- `harness-supervisor-judge-model` — Model that judges how a new session starts, as PROVIDER:NAME, or `auto`.
- `harness-supervisor-step-budget` — Tool calls a supervising turn makes before it is told to submit its plan.
- `harness-supervisor-tasks` — How the sessions of tasks start: supervising, hands-on, or judged.
- `harness-supervisor-tiers` — Models the workers of a supervisor's plan run on, by tier of the step.
